page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Ax.Flex.4-16 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance powered by an Ampere AmpereOne-M processor built on the 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. Configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, the instance maintains a direct 1:1 core-to-thread execution model without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 16.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a resource ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per execution core.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local NVMe or solid-state storage, necessitating remote block volumes for persistent disk drives and application storage. Acceleration hardware is omitted, with zero GPUs present. Network integration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external ingress and egress routing.

With a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, the configuration emphasizes computational density over vast memory capacity. This resource profile offers cost-effective execution for scale-out compute tasks, compiled Arm application testing, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and web servers that do not require expansive memory footprints or dedicated local scratch disks.

Given its dedicated core execution and lean memory allocation, this virtual machine offers efficient hardware density and predictability for Arm-native development, continuous integration pipelines, web tier hosting, and general lightweight computational jobs.
